approach.label: How I work
approach.body: Instead of polishing static slides, I diagnose where automation or interfaces break people's trust, design clear refusal and recovery paths, and build running software or hardware prototypes to test those choices early.

1.b: Find where people hesitate, misclick, or stop trusting an automated workflow.

2.b: Reject flashy auto-shortcuts when explicit confirmation or leaving blanks blank protects the user.

3.b: Build real Next.js, Electron, extension, or ESP32 prototypes backed by automated tests.

4.b: Separate measured device/repo verification from outside participant testing still left to run.

designPrinciples.title: Friction First
designPrinciples.description: Start from real failure modes, false-positive costs, and broken user expectations before drawing components.

designPrinciples.title: Falsify Early
designPrinciples.description: Ship working firmware, extensions, or UI state machines early so brittle assumptions break in testing rather than shipping.

designPrinciples.title: Accessible & Tactile
designPrinciples.description: Keyboard flow, >= 24px targets, AAA typography contrast, and 0ms reduced-motion parity belong in the spec from day one.

designPrinciples.title: Calibrated Evidence
designPrinciples.description: Separate bench checks and synthetic runs from cohort studies; state every unverified limit plainly.

headline.text: I design interactions that help people stay oriented.

about.p1: I'm finishing my Master of Interaction Design at The University of Queensland in November 2026 after earning a BSc (Hons) in Computer Science (2:1) at Swansea University in Wales. Having both engineering and design training keeps me grounded in what software and hardware can actually uphold under latency, permissions, and human fatigue.
about.p2: My work focuses on complex human-system boundaries: where AI tools overreach user confidence, where multi-player hardware breaks solo silence, and where workflows hide failure or privacy risk. Instead of ending at static slides, I ship working prototypes in TypeScript, Electron, Chrome extensions, or ESP32 C++ so the rules can fail honestly and be revised.
about.p3: In AI-assisted builds, I keep clear ownership: I define the human tension, the rejected shortcuts, the refusal limits, and the real hardware or Playwright acceptance checks — treating generated code as a draft to be interrogated rather than truth by default.
about.p4: If you have a complex interaction problem or graduate opening, write directly and I will respond promptly.

1.b: If a study never challenges a design choice, it didn't earn its time.

2.b: The best interaction gets out of the way so people can act with confidence.

3.b: Empty states, recovery paths, and physical confirmations — that's where trust actually lives.

4.b: Writing down constraints and assumptions keeps everyone aligned long after a meeting ends.
